# Tests s3t is expected to fail — the conformance gate.
#
# s3t runs the whole ported suite on every pull request and fails if anything
# outside this file fails, or if anything inside it passes. The list can
# therefore only shrink: a newly passing test shows up on the pull request that
# made it pass, and a newly failing one is never silently absorbed.
#
# Read it inverted: everything not listed here passes. 49 of the
# 301 tests s3t currently ports are listed.
#
# When a change makes a test pass, delete its line in the same change. CI names
# the lines to delete. Do not add lines to make CI green: a new line is a
# regression someone is choosing to keep, and it needs a reason beside it.

# --- Full ACL grammar (27) --------------------------------------------------
#
# PUT ?acl reduces an AccessControlPolicy body to the nearest canned level, so
# grants to specific users are accepted and ignored, and the access matrix
# these tests walk does not hold. Out of scope (#130): per-credential grants
# cover the need this server has.

s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_access_bucket_private_object_publicread

# --- SSE-KMS (13) -------------------------------------------------------------
#
# aws:kms is refused rather than accepted and ignored. These passed until
# SSE-S3 landed, and passed for a bad reason: the header was accepted, the
# object written in the clear, and the client told its request was honored.
# Refusing makes them fail honestly. SSE-KMS needs a key service and is out of
# scope (#133).
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_copy_enc[sse-kms-unencrypted-STANDARD-STANDARD-1024]
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_copy_enc[sse-kms-unencrypted-STANDARD-STANDARD-1048576]
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_copy_enc[sse-kms-unencrypted-STANDARD-STANDARD-1]
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_copy_enc[sse-kms-unencrypted-STANDARD-STANDARD-8388608]
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_copy_part_enc[sse-kms-unencrypted-STANDARD-STANDARD-8388608]
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_sse_kms_multipart_invalid_chunks_1
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_sse_kms_multipart_invalid_chunks_2
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_sse_kms_multipart_upload
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_sse_kms_present
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_sse_kms_transfer_13b
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_sse_kms_transfer_1MB
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_sse_kms_transfer_1b
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_sse_kms_transfer_1kb

# --- Bucket default encryption applied to writes (2) ----------------------
#
# The ?encryption default is stored and reported, and these two check that it
# is also applied to a write that names no algorithm, on HEAD and on multipart.
# The wiring exists per request and server-wide; the bucket default is not
# consulted on these two paths yet (#124 follow-up).
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_sse_s3_default_method_head
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_sse_s3_default_multipart_upload

# --- Client-visible checksums (7) --------------------------------------------
#
# x-amz-checksum-* is accepted and ignored: the digest is neither verified nor
# reported, so a wrong one is stored and acknowledged as if it had been
# checked. #120.
#
# Listed before the tests exist at the pinned S3T_REF — s3t ignores an entry
# naming a test it does not carry — so that the gate stays honest the moment
# the pin moves rather than going red on the bump.
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_object_checksum_crc64nvme
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_object_checksum_sha256
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_multipart_use_cksum_helper_crc32
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_multipart_use_cksum_helper_crc32c
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_multipart_use_cksum_helper_crc64nvme
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_multipart_use_cksum_helper_sha1
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_multipart_use_cksum_helper_sha256
